cuetRelevance.pyqFrequency: Appears in 100% of tested CUET shifts (8-10 questions per shift)

summary30Seconds: On Admission: New partner brings capital and Premium for Goodwill, which is distributed among old partners in their Sacrificing Ratio (Old Ratio - New Ratio).
Revaluation Account (Nominal A/c): Debit decrease in asset & increase in liability; Credit increase in asset & decrease in liability. Profit/Loss transferred to Old Partners in Old Ratio.

On Retirement/Death: Gaining Ratio = New Ratio - Old Ratio. Retiring/deceased partner's share of goodwill is compensated by gaining partners in gaining ratio. Interim profit to deceased partner is debited to P&L Suspense Account.

coreConcepts.title: Sacrificing vs Gaining Ratio & Revaluation Account
coreConcepts.content:
**Ratios**:
- **Sacrificing Ratio (Admission)**:
  $$\text{Sacrificing Ratio} = \text{Old Ratio} - \text{New Ratio}$$
  Used strictly to distribute the incoming partner's **Premium for Goodwill** among sacrificing partners.
- **Gaining Ratio (Retirement / Death)**:
  $$\text{Gaining Ratio} = \text{New Ratio} - \text{Old Ratio}$$
  Used to debit gaining partners' capital accounts to compensate the retiring/deceased partner for their goodwill share.

**Revaluation Account (Profit and Loss Adjustment Account)**:
A nominal account prepared at the time of reconstitution to revalue assets and reassess liabilities:
- **Debit side**: Decrease in value of assets, increase in value of liabilities, unrecorded liabilities.
- **Credit side**: Increase in value of assets, decrease in value of liabilities, unrecorded assets.
- **Balancing Figure**: Net profit or net loss transferred to **Old Partners' Capital Accounts in their Old Profit Sharing Ratio**.
ncertPointers: Expenses on revaluation paid by the firm on behalf of a partner are debited to Partner's Capital A/c.
Workmen Compensation Reserve (WCR): Excess reserve over actual liability is distributed to old partners in old ratio.
Investment Fluctuation Reserve (IFR): Used to absorb fall in market value of investments below book value; remainder distributed in old ratio.

coreConcepts.title: Goodwill Treatment on Admission & Retirement
coreConcepts.content:
**On Admission**:
1. When premium for goodwill is paid **privately**: No journal entry in firm's books.
2. When brought in cash:
   $$\text{Bank A/c Dr. to Premium for Goodwill A/c}$$
   $$\text{Premium for Goodwill A/c Dr. to Sacrificing Partners' Capital A/cs [Sacrificing Ratio]}$$
3. When new partner cannot bring premium in cash:
   $$\text{New Partner's Current A/c Dr. to Sacrificing Partners' Capital A/cs}$$
4. Existing goodwill in balance sheet:
   $$\text{Old Partners' Capital A/cs Dr. [Old Ratio] to Goodwill A/c}$$

**On Retirement / Death**:
Goodwill is not brought into books. Retiring partner's share is adjusted through remaining partners:
$$\text{Gaining Partners' Capital A/cs Dr. [Gaining Ratio] to Retiring/Deceased Partner's Capital A/c}$$
ncertPointers: Hidden Goodwill: Total capital of new firm based on new partner's investment minus actual combined capital of all partners.
If a continuing partner sacrifices on retirement, their capital account is ALSO credited along with retiring partner.

coreConcepts.title: Death of a Partner: Interim Profit & Section 37
coreConcepts.content:
**Calculation of Deceased Partner's Share of Profit till Date of Death**:
1. **On Time Basis**:
   $$\text{Profit till Death} = \text{Previous Year / Average Profit} \times \frac{\text{Days / Months till Death}}{12 / 365}$$
   $$\text{Deceased Partner's Share} = \text{Profit till Death} \times \text{Deceased Partner's Ratio}$$
2. **On Turnover / Sales Basis**:
   $$\text{Estimated Profit} = \frac{\text{Previous Year Profit}}{\text{Previous Year Sales}} \times \text{Sales till Date of Death}$$
   $$\text{Deceased Partner's Share} = \text{Estimated Profit} \times \text{Deceased Partner's Ratio}$$

**Journal Entry (if PSR of continuing partners does not change)**:
$$\text{Profit and Loss Suspense A/c Dr. to Deceased Partner's Capital A/c}$$
*(If PSR changes, it is adjusted via Gaining Partners' Capital A/cs Dr. in Gaining Ratio).*

**Section 37 of Indian Partnership Act, 1932**:
If the outgoing/deceased partner's dues are not settled immediately and no agreement exists, the executor is entitled at their option to:
- **Interest @ 6% p.a.** on unpaid balance, OR
- Such share of subsequent profits earned as attributable to the use of their capital.
ncertPointers: All balances of deceased partner's capital account are transferred to Deceased Partner's Executor's Account, not paid directly to the partner.

keyFormulasAndTables.name: Section 37 Settlement Options
keyFormulasAndTables.formula: \text{Option A: Interest @ 6% p.a. on unpaid dues} \quad \text{vs} \quad \text{Option B: Proportionate share of post-death profits}
keyFormulasAndTables.applicationCondition: Delayed settlement of deceased partner's dues

workedExamples.question: A and B are partners sharing profits in the ratio 3:2. They admit C into partnership for 1/5th share which he acquires entirely from A. Calculate the new profit-sharing ratio.
solutionSteps: Step 2: C's share = 1/5, acquired entirely from A.
Step 3: A's new share = Old share - Share sacrificed = 3/5 - 1/5 = 2/5.
Step 5: C's share = 1/5. New ratio A : B : C = 2/5 : 2/5 : 1/5 = 2 : 2 : 1. Option A is exact.

workedExamples.question: P, Q, and R share profits in the ratio 5:3:2. R dies on 30th June 2025. Accounts are closed on 31st March every year. Sales for the year ended 31st March 2025 were ₹6,00,000 and profit was ₹1,20,000. Sales from 1st April 2025 to 30th June 2025 were ₹2,00,000. Calculate R's share of profit till the date of death.
solutionSteps: Step 1: Profit percentage on sales in previous year = (₹1,20,000 / ₹6,00,000) × 100 = 20%.
Step 2: Estimated profit for the 3 months (sales = ₹2,00,000) = ₹2,00,000 × 20% = ₹40,000.
Step 4: R's share of profit till death = ₹40,000 × (2/10) = ₹8,000.

howCuetAsks.typicalStem: A, B, and C are partners sharing in ratio 4:3:2. B retires and his share is taken over by A and C equally. What is the new ratio?
Which account is debited to record the interim share of profit given to a deceased partner when the continuing partners' ratio does not change?

commonTraps.misconception: Distributing revaluation profit among ALL partners including the newly admitted partner.
commonTraps.correctUnderstanding: Revaluation profit belongs strictly to the **OLD partners in their OLD profit-sharing ratio** because the appreciation occurred prior to admission.

commonTraps.misconception: Confusing credit of premium to sacrificing partners with actual cash withdrawal.
commonTraps.correctUnderstanding: Crediting premium increases capital. Partners may withdraw cash only if the problem explicitly says 'and was withdrawn by the old partners' (then Partners' Capital Dr. to Bank).

mnemonicsAndShortcuts.title: Sacrificing vs Gaining Formula
mnemonicsAndShortcuts.mnemonic: SON: Sacrificing = Old - New. GNO: Gaining = New - Old.
mnemonicsAndShortcuts.explanation: Simple acronym to avoid reversing fractions during exam pressure.

mnemonicsAndShortcuts.title: Revaluation Golden Rule
mnemonicsAndShortcuts.mnemonic: Good news on Credit (+), Bad news on Debit (-).
mnemonicsAndShortcuts.explanation: Asset increase/Liability decrease = Credit; Asset decrease/Liability increase = Debit.

practiceQuestions.question: When a new partner brings cash for goodwill, the amount is credited to:
practiceQuestions.explanation: When cash is brought in for goodwill by the new partner, the entry is Cash/Bank A/c Dr. to Premium for Goodwill A/c.

practiceQuestions.question: Premium for goodwill brought in by a newly admitted partner is shared by old partners in their:
practiceQuestions.explanation: The premium for goodwill is compensation paid by incoming partner to existing partners for surrendering part of their profit share; hence it is credited in Sacrificing Ratio.

practiceQuestions.question: Revaluation Account is a:
practiceQuestions.explanation: Revaluation Account is a nominal account prepared to ascertain net gain or loss arising from revaluation of assets and reassessment of liabilities.

practiceQuestions.question: At the time of admission of a partner, unrecorded investment of ₹10,000 is accounted for by:
practiceQuestions.explanation: An unrecorded asset increases the net worth of the business; hence Unrecorded Investment A/c is debited and Revaluation Account is credited.

practiceQuestions.question: X, Y, and Z are partners sharing profits in the ratio 3:2:1. Z retires. The gaining ratio of X and Y will be:
practiceQuestions.explanation: If no information is given regarding the acquisition of retiring partner's share, the remaining partners share profits in their old relative ratio (3:2), which is also their gaining ratio.

practiceQuestions.question: Under Section 37 of the Indian Partnership Act 1932, if the dues of a deceased partner are not settled immediately, the executor is entitled to interest on the unpaid amount at:
practiceQuestions.explanation: Under Section 37, the outgoing/deceased partner's executor is entitled to interest @ 6% p.a. on the unsettled amount or a proportionate share of subsequent profits.

practiceQuestions.question: A and B share profits in ratio 3:2. C is admitted with 1/4th share. C brings ₹40,000 as capital. The total capital of the new firm based on C's share is:
practiceQuestions.explanation: Total capital = C's capital × reciprocal of C's share = ₹40,000 × (4/1) = ₹1,60,000.

practiceQuestions.question: General Reserve appearing in the Balance Sheet at the time of admission of a new partner is transferred to:

options.text: Old Partners' Capital Accounts in Old Ratio
All Partners' Capital Accounts in New Ratio

practiceQuestions.explanation: General Reserve is an accumulated profit created out of past earnings before admission; it belongs solely to old partners and is transferred to their Capital Accounts in their old ratio.

practiceQuestions.question: On the death of a partner, the balance in his capital account is finally transferred to:
practiceQuestions.explanation: Since the deceased partner is no longer alive, the net amount payable is transferred to Deceased Partner's Executor's Account.

practiceQuestions.question: If continuing partners decide to change their profit sharing ratio among themselves after retirement of a partner, the goodwill of the retiring partner is debited to continuing partners in:
practiceQuestions.explanation: Whenever there is a change in profit share, the gaining partners compensate the sacrificing/retiring partner in their gaining ratio (Gaining Partners' Capital Dr. to Retiring Partner's Capital).
